system.name: T3 Code
system.description: Desktop, web and mobile apps that control coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode running on your own machine, through one local server per machine.

corpus.included: The whole pingdotgg/t3code repository at this revision and its history since 2026-05-25: apps, packages, infra, native helpers, docs, scripts and configuration.
corpus.excluded: The vendored repositories in .repos/ (alchemy-effect and effect, counted as dependencies), the lockfile, generated code and vendored binaries; no secrets were found.

consumers.name: Developer
consumers.description: A person who runs coding agents through T3 Code from a desktop, browser, phone or terminal, including the scripts, bots and outside agents they connect.

consumers.name: Guest
consumers.description: A teammate who opens a guest link to follow one thread in a browser and ask the agent questions, without an account.

consumers.name: Machine administrator
consumers.description: A person who sets defaults, locks and limits for every user of T3 Code on a machine through a managed policy.

providers.name: T3 Code
providers.description: The product the developer uses: apps on every device, a server on each machine that runs the agents, and the T3 Connect service that links them.

parts.name: t3.codes website
parts.why: Static pages and download links built from GitHub releases (apps/marketing); keeps no state and decides nothing, so it is part of an interface.

parts.name: t3 npm launcher
parts.why: Runs the right t3 release for npx (scripts/npm-launcher) and passes the command on, so it is part of the command line interface.

parts.name: Wire contracts
parts.why: Schema definitions of every API between the parts (packages/contracts), a library with no runtime logic of its own.

parts.name: Shared utilities
parts.why: Helpers used by every part (packages/shared), a library.

parts.name: Native helpers
parts.why: Small native programs for terminal parsing, window capture, process sampling, browser secrets and Apple speech (native/*, apps/desktop/gnome-extension), adapters to the operating system.

parts.name: Shared task cache
parts.why: A build cache for maintainers and CI (infra/task-cache), engineering tooling.

components.name: Client app
components.description: The web, desktop-window and mobile apps, built on one client runtime, that connect to environments and the relay and keep the saved environments.

parts.name: Connection runtime
parts.why: Keeps the saved environments, their credentials and the T3 Connect sign-in and owns reconnects (packages/client-runtime/src/connection, authorization, relay); it passes the component test but is the only part that does, so the app stays closed.

parts.name: Shared client state
parts.why: Caches of the server's threads and projects and commands queued while offline (packages/client-runtime/src/state, platform, operations); the environment's state wins on reconnect, so it mirrors the server rather than owning state.

parts.name: Web UI
parts.why: Presents the capabilities in browsers and the desktop window (apps/web); drafts, prompt stash and the machine chosen for a draft are presentation state and interactions, part of the interface.

parts.name: Mobile UI
parts.why: Presents the capabilities on iOS and Android (apps/mobile/src), part of the interface.

parts.name: Voice input and device viewer
parts.why: Present recording and a device's video stream (packages/client-runtime/src/voice-input, device); transcription is done by the phone or the environment.

parts.name: Mobile native modules
parts.why: Adapters to iOS and Android for widgets, Live Activities, push tokens, terminal and highlighting (apps/mobile/modules).

components.name: Desktop shell
components.description: The Electron main process of the desktop app, which runs environment servers on this computer, hosts the desktop browser and captures windows.

parts.name: Desktop updates
parts.why: Download and install new app versions and update connected servers (apps/desktop/src/updates); updating the system itself, tooling.

parts.name: Desktop settings stores
parts.why: Files the window persists through the bridge, such as client settings and the saved environments (apps/desktop/src/settings, ipc/methods/connectionCatalog.ts); storage for the client app, not a capability of its own.

parts.name: Renderer telemetry
parts.why: Records the window's history for diagnostics (apps/desktop/src/telemetry), tooling.

parts.name: App lifecycle and handlers
parts.why: Startup, windows, menus, the t3 app command shim, protocol and web-link handling, sign-in redirects and managed policy reading (apps/desktop/src/app, window, electron); wiring.

parts.name: Bridge transport
parts.why: IPC channels and the preload that expose the desktop bridge to the window (apps/desktop/src/ipc, preload.ts); passes requests on.

parts.name: macOS permission helpers and Apple Speech adapter
parts.why: Adapters to operating system permissions and the speech recognizer (apps/desktop/src/permissions, speech).

components.name: Server launcher
components.description: Starts, exposes and stops the environment servers this desktop runs: locally, in WSL, or on a remote host over SSH.

parts.name: Local backend
parts.why: Variant that runs the bundled server as a child process (backend/DesktopBackendManager.ts, DesktopBackendPool.ts).

parts.name: Network exposure
parts.why: Network access and Tailscale Serve for the local server (backend/DesktopServerExposure.ts), state of the same launcher kept in app settings.

parts.name: WSL backend
parts.why: Variant that runs the server in a WSL distro through the same pool (wsl/*).

parts.name: SSH environments
parts.why: Variant that starts or reuses a server on a remote host (ssh/*, packages/ssh).

components.name: Desktop browser
components.description: Hosts preview browser tabs in the desktop window, with browser profiles, imported cookies and passkeys, and tunnels localhost for remote environments.

parts.name: Tab manager
parts.why: Keeps the webviews of the tabs (preview/Manager.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Profiles and cookie import
parts.why: Imports cookies into the same Electron sessions the tabs use (preview/BrowserImport/*, BrowserSession.ts), so it shares the tabs' store.

parts.name: Passkeys
parts.why: Passkey backend for pages in the tabs (preview/Passkey*.ts), same browser sessions.

parts.name: Loopback tunnel and CDP relay
parts.why: Mechanics that reach a remote host's localhost and relay the server's browser commands (preview/LoopbackTunnel.ts, CdpRelay.ts).

parts.name: Annotation and recording
parts.why: Element picking, annotations and recordings inside tabs (preview/Annotation*.ts, Recording*.ts), interactions.

components.name: SnapShots
components.description: Captures the window you work in, with its accessibility data, and hands it to the window to attach to a draft.

parts.name: Pending captures
parts.why: Keeps captures until the window takes them (snapShot/DesktopSnapShot.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Platform capture variants
parts.why: macOS, Windows, GNOME, KDE, Hyprland, Niri and portal capture (snapShot/*SnapShot.ts, native/kde-snap-shot, native/hyprland-snap-shot, apps/desktop/gnome-extension), variants of one capture.

parts.name: Shortcut and accessibility workers
parts.why: Processes that listen for the shortcut and read accessibility data (snapShot/*Process.ts, *Worker.ts), helpers.

components.name: Environment server
components.description: The server on each machine that owns projects, threads, agent processes, terminals, Git and every durable record, and serves the apps, outside agents and the relay.

parts.name: RPC and HTTP transports
parts.why: Decode a request, call one service method and map its errors (apps/server/src/ws.ts, http.ts; docs/internals/02_effect-services.md), part of the environment API interface.

parts.name: Command line
parts.why: Passes commands to services or to a running server (apps/server/src/cli), part of the t3 command line interface.

parts.name: Service launcher and updates
parts.why: Installs, supervises and updates the server itself (apps/server/src/serviceLauncher.ts, cloud/service*.ts, cloud/selfUpdate.ts, desktopUpdate), tooling that works on the system.

parts.name: Persistence
parts.why: SQLite storage and migrations for the components (apps/server/src/persistence).

parts.name: Process spawning
parts.why: Library that launches child processes (apps/server/src/process).

parts.name: Analytics, feedback and diagnostics
parts.why: Report on the system itself to maintainers and to the diagnostics pages (apps/server/src/telemetry, feedback, observability, diagnostics), tooling.

parts.name: Server wiring
parts.why: Composes the services and starts the server (apps/server/src/server.ts, bootstrap.ts, config.ts, bin*.ts).

components.name: Orchestration
components.description: Decides and records every change to projects and threads as events, runs the side effects after commit, and streams threads to their readers.

parts.name: Decider
parts.why: Turns commands into events from current state without I/O (orchestration-v2/Orchestrator.ts, CommandPolicy.ts, RuntimePolicy.ts); shares the event store.

parts.name: Event store and projections
parts.why: Commits events, projections, receipts and the outbox in one transaction (EventSink.ts, ProjectionStore.ts, ProjectStore.ts, EffectOutbox.ts); the store every other part writes through.

parts.name: Effect worker and run services
parts.why: Run side effects after commit and feed results back (EffectWorker.ts, RunExecutionService.ts, CheckpointService.ts); they write through the same EventSink.

parts.name: Provider session manager
parts.why: Keeps live agent sessions bound to threads and ingests their events (ProviderSessionManager.ts, ProviderEventIngestor.ts); commits through the same EventSink.

parts.name: Read streams and search
parts.why: Stream and search the projections (ShellStream.ts, ThreadStream.ts, ThreadSearch.ts, CommandOutputHub.ts).

parts.name: Projects
parts.why: Create, clone and set up projects and import agent sessions (apps/server/src/project); they commit through EventSink and ProjectStore, so they share the store.

parts.name: Guest view
parts.why: Signs guest tokens bound to a share kept in the thread projection and serves the guest page's data (apps/server/src/guest).

parts.name: Attachments and assets
parts.why: Files of messages and signed media URLs (apps/server/src/assets, attachmentStore.ts).

parts.name: MCP app context, triage and keep-awake
parts.why: Thread-scoped helpers (apps/server/src/mcpApps, triage, background).

components.name: Agent providers
components.description: Runs each configured coding agent behind one adapter contract, from installing and signing in to opening sessions, and writes text and reads usage through them.

parts.name: Provider sign-in coordinator
parts.why: Passes sign-in steps to each driver's auth controller (provider/ProviderAuthService.ts, CodexChatGptAuth.ts, AntigravityAuth.ts); drivers keep the credentials through ProviderHost.

parts.name: Text generation
parts.why: Writes titles, commit messages and descriptions by calling drivers or model APIs (apps/server/src/textGeneration); keeps nothing.

parts.name: Usage
parts.why: Reads providers' history and limits and derives a view (apps/server/src/usage, provider/*UsageLimits.ts); only a scan cache.

parts.name: Resource sampling
parts.why: Measures host and agent process load (apps/server/src/resourceTelemetry, native/resource-monitor).

components.name: Agent drivers
components.description: One driver per kind of coding agent that keeps each instance's native sessions, processes and credentials and translates its protocol.

parts.name: Claude, Codex and Antigravity drivers
parts.why: Variants built into the server (provider/Drivers/*, orchestration-v2/Adapters/*).

parts.name: Cursor, OpenCode, Grok, Kiro, Pi, Muse and fx drivers
parts.why: Variants in their own packages (packages/provider-*).

parts.name: ACP and ACP Registry drivers
parts.why: Variants for any ACP agent (packages/provider-acp, provider-acp-registry, effect-acp).

parts.name: Driver SDK
parts.why: The shared contract and helpers drivers build on (packages/provider-core), a library.

components.name: Provider registry
components.description: Builds the live provider instances from settings, checks their status and models, and decides which instances are enabled and ready.

parts.name: Model catalogs and manifest
parts.why: Reference data the registry reads (provider/ModelManifest.ts, model-manifest.json, *ModelCatalog.ts).

parts.name: Status cache
parts.why: Storage of the last status of each instance (provider/providerStatusCache.ts).

components.name: Agent installation
components.description: Installs and updates agent CLIs and managed runtimes, only through an installer that provably owns them.

parts.name: Installation gate
parts.why: Drains running executions before an update (provider/ProviderInstallationGate.ts), a step of installing.

parts.name: Managed runtimes
parts.why: Codex and Antigravity managed runtime variants (provider/CodexManagedRuntime.ts, AntigravityInstallation.ts).

components.name: Access control
components.description: Issues and revokes the environment's sessions, pairing links, agent sign-ins and T3 Connect device approvals, and authorizes every call.

parts.name: Sessions and pairing
parts.why: One store of sessions, pairing links and approved devices (auth/SessionStore.ts, PairingGrantStore.ts, persistence/Auth*.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Per-call authorization
parts.why: Checks each RPC's scope against the grants in that store (auth/RpcAuthorization.ts).

parts.name: MCP sign-in
parts.why: OAuth for outside agents that issues sessions into the same store (auth/McpOAuth.ts).

parts.name: Signing and secret storage
parts.why: Keys, DPoP proofs, replay markers and the server secret store (auth/PayloadSigner.ts, ServerSecretStore.ts, dpop.ts), library and storage.

parts.name: Environment identity
parts.why: The environment's id and advertised routes (apps/server/src/environment), an identifier.

components.name: Workspace
components.description: Decides and prepares the folder each thread works in, runs a project's worktree layout commands only as a person approved them, and reads and writes project files.

parts.name: Task folders
parts.why: Keeps task folders and layout approvals (workspace/TaskFolders.ts, TaskFolderStore.ts, LayoutCommandApproval*.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Workspace files
parts.why: Adapter over the filesystem with path rules and an in-memory search index (workspace/WorkspaceFileSystem.ts, WorkspaceSearchIndex.ts).

parts.name: Storage cleanup
parts.why: Clean-up job for worktrees and logs (storageCleanup.ts).

components.name: Git
components.description: Runs Git for threads: status, branches, worktrees, commits, pushes and the hidden checkpoints behind diffs and restore.

parts.name: Git driver
parts.why: Adapter to the git command line (vcs/GitVcsDriver*.ts, VcsDriver.ts, VcsDriverRegistry.ts).

components.name: Checkpoints
components.description: Captures, diffs and restores workspace states as hidden Git refs that never add commits to the user's branch.

parts.name: Checkpoint store
parts.why: Writes and reads the hidden refs (checkpointing/CheckpointStore.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Diff queries
parts.why: Read diffs between checkpoints (checkpointing/CheckpointDiffQuery.ts, Diffs.ts).

components.name: Git actions
components.description: Decides commit, push and pull request sequences and branch changes for threads, and keeps repository status up to date.

parts.name: Status broadcaster
parts.why: Keeps status subscriptions and fetch timing (vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts).

parts.name: Review service
parts.why: Reads diff previews and branch commits (review/ReviewService.ts).

components.name: Code host integration
components.description: Connects projects to code hosting services and Linear: sign-ins, cloning and publishing, pull requests and issues.

parts.name: Forge drivers
parts.why: Adapters to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Forgejo, GitCafe, TanStack Source and Cursor Origin, variants of one contract (packages/source-control-*).

parts.name: Forge definitions
parts.why: Definitions the server and every client load, kept free of UI and server code by a lint rule (packages/source-control-definitions, packages/source-control-*/src/shared; vite.config.ts), a library.

components.name: Code host connections
components.description: Keeps the code host sign-ins, decides which forge serves a repository, and clones and publishes repositories through it.

parts.name: Repository service
parts.why: Looks up, clones and publishes through the chosen forge (sourceControl/SourceControlRepositoryService.ts), passes requests on.

components.name: Pull requests
components.description: Lists, reviews, updates and merges pull requests, keeps which files you viewed and the review guides, and watches thread pull requests.

serves.area: Work with pull requests and issues
Act on issues and pull requests

parts.name: Watch and review guides
parts.why: Watches and review-guide generation of the same component (pullRequest/PullRequestWatchService.ts, PullRequestReviewGuideService.ts).

components.name: Issues
components.description: Lists and changes issues from forges and Linear, and keeps tracker accounts and which teams each project shows.

serves.area: Work with pull requests and issues
Act on issues and pull requests

parts.name: Linear driver
parts.why: Adapter to Linear (packages/issue-tracker-linear).

components.name: Scheduled tasks
components.description: Keeps scheduled tasks and their webhook deliveries and starts their runs on time or when a webhook arrives.

parts.name: Task store and runner
parts.why: Writes the tasks and deliveries (scheduledTasks/ScheduledTaskService.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Timing
parts.why: Decides when the next task is due (scheduling/Scheduler.ts), on the same records.

parts.name: Webhook route, filter and dedupe
parts.why: Verifies, filters and de-duplicates webhook calls (scheduledTasks/webhook*.ts) on the same tables.

components.name: Workflows
components.description: Runs workflow scripts as durable runs that survive restarts, with steps, questions, triggers and agent steps.

parts.name: Workflow store
parts.why: Keeps runs, steps, waits, triggers and hooks (workflows/WorkflowStore.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Engine and runtime
parts.why: Execute steps and retries on the same store (workflows/WorkflowEngine.ts, WorkflowRuntime.ts).

parts.name: Triggers and agent steps
parts.why: Schedules, webhooks, forge events and agent threads of the same runs (workflows/triggers.ts, WorkflowForge.ts, WorkflowAgents.ts).

parts.name: Script API
parts.why: The workflow, step and ask functions scripts call (workflows/api.ts, workflow.ts), a library for workflow authors.

components.name: Linked environments
components.description: Keeps links to other environments, forwards agents' calls to them under a mode ceiling, and relays their threads read-only.

parts.name: Link store
parts.why: Keeps the links (peer/PeerLinks.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Forwarding and delegation
parts.why: Applies mode ceilings and link fencing to forwarded calls (peer/PeerForwarding.ts, RemoteDelegation.ts).

parts.name: MCP client and thread relay
parts.why: Adapter to the other machine's MCP endpoint and a read-only stream proxy (peer/PeerMcpClient.ts, PeerThreadRelay.ts).

parts.name: Pairing and link requests
parts.why: Link cards waiting for a person and pairing over a link, on the same link records (peer/PeerLinkRequests.ts, PeerClientPairing.ts).

components.name: T3 Connect link
components.description: Keeps the environment's link to T3 Connect and its managed tunnel, checks the relay's proofs and mints credentials for relayed clients.

parts.name: Link state and proofs
parts.why: Cloud credentials and relay proof checks (cloud/CloudLink.ts, CliState.ts, CliTokenManager.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Tunnel runtime
parts.why: Runs cloudflared for the managed tunnel (cloud/ManagedEndpointRuntime.ts), an adapter.

parts.name: Activity publisher and hook waker
parts.why: Pass agent activity and held-webhook wake-ups on to the relay (relay/AgentAwarenessRelay.ts, HeldHooksWaker.ts).

parts.name: Reachability checks
parts.why: Diagnostics of the link (cloud/ConnectReachability.ts, linkChecks.ts).

components.name: Terminals
components.description: Keeps the shells opened on the machine for threads and projects, with their history.

parts.name: Terminal manager
parts.why: Keeps sessions and history (terminal/Manager.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: PTY adapter and output protocol
parts.why: Adapter to node-pty and the output format (terminal/NodePtyAdapter.ts, OutputProtocol.ts).

components.name: Browser
components.description: Keeps the environment's browser tabs, which people and agents share, and drives them in a headless browser or in the desktop app.

parts.name: Tab manager
parts.why: Keeps the tabs (preview/Manager.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Browser hosts
parts.why: Headless Chromium and the desktop browser channel, variants the tab manager drives (preview/ServerBrowser*.ts, DesktopBrowserChannel.ts).

parts.name: Local server discovery and loopback tunnel
parts.why: Helpers that find local servers and tunnel localhost (preview/PortScanner.ts, PreviewTunnel.ts).

parts.name: Visual replies
parts.why: Checks and publishes agents' HTML pages into attachment files with the same browser (apps/server/src/htmlRender); no store of its own.

parts.name: Agent automation broker
parts.why: Passes agents' browser actions to tabs (mcp/PreviewAutomationBroker.ts).

components.name: Devices
components.description: Keeps the device hub and the simulators and emulators people and agents use, on this machine or on remote device hosts.

parts.name: Device service
parts.why: Keeps hub and device state (device/DeviceService.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Device hosts
parts.why: Local, SSH, Simlock and EAS variants (device/*DeviceHost.ts), adapters.

parts.name: Device tool setup
parts.why: Installs device tools on demand (device/DeviceToolchain.ts, deviceToolMaintenance.ts).

parts.name: Agent device shim
parts.why: The agent-device command agents run, which passes requests to the device service (device/AgentDeviceShim.ts).

components.name: Secrets
components.description: Resolves secret references through password managers, keeps secret setting values, and holds agents' secret requests until a person answers.

parts.name: Secret requests
parts.why: Pending requests saved into the server secret store (secrets/SecretRequests.ts).

parts.name: Resolver and checks
parts.why: Read references through a secret provider (secrets/SecretResolver.ts, SecretCheck.ts).

parts.name: Stored setting values
parts.why: Secret values of settings in the same store (settingsSecrets.ts).

parts.name: 1Password adapter
parts.why: Adapter to the op CLI and Connect servers (packages/secret-provider-onepassword).

components.name: Settings and policy
components.description: Keeps the environment's settings and keybindings and enforces the administrator's managed policy over them.

components.name: Environment settings
components.description: Keeps settings.json and keybindings and gives each setting's effective value through defaults, environment and project layers.

parts.name: Settings file
parts.why: ServerSettingsService (serverSettings.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Keybindings and theme
parts.why: Files of the same settings owner (keybindings.ts, environmentTheme.ts).

components.name: Policy enforcement
components.description: Reads the administrator's policy once at startup and alone decides its locks and limits, such as the broadest permission mode or which clients may connect.

parts.name: Limits, settings and providers rules
parts.why: Pieces of the one policy (policy/managedLimits.ts, managedSettings.ts, managedProviders.ts, managedUpdates.ts).

components.name: Voice transcription
components.description: Downloads and selects speech models and transcribes dictation on the environment, locally or through a model API.

parts.name: Speech service and model store
parts.why: One model store (speech/SpeechService.ts, SpeechModelStore.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Engines and cloud speech
parts.why: Adapters to local engines and model APIs (speech/native.ts, silero.ts, CloudSpeech.ts).

parts.name: Transcript clean-up
parts.why: Uses text generation (speech/postProcessing.ts).

components.name: Agent tools
components.description: The environment's MCP endpoint: decides which agent may call which tool under which mode, and streams environment events to bots.

components.name: Tool server
components.description: Registers every T3 tool, checks who may call it and under which mode ceiling, and keeps in-thread agents' MCP sessions.

parts.name: Tool handlers
parts.why: Decode a tool call and call one service (mcp/toolkits/*), pass requests on.

parts.name: Thread tools service
parts.why: Launch, send, wait and delegation logic over Orchestration (mcp/OrchestratorMcpService.ts), part of the same tool server.

components.name: Agent events
components.description: Keeps the latest environment milestones and bots' event subscriptions in memory and delivers events by stream or webhook.

parts.name: Milestone hub
parts.why: Keeps recent milestones and subscriptions (milestones/MilestoneHub.ts); the core of this component.

parts.name: Webhook transport
parts.why: Delivers to public https receivers only (mcp/McpWebhookTransport.ts).

components.name: T3 Connect relay
components.description: The hosted T3 Connect service that links environments to accounts, gives them public tunnels, admits clients, holds webhooks and pushes notifications to phones.

parts.name: Relay API handlers
parts.why: HTTP handlers that pass requests to the components (infra/relay/src/http/Api.ts), part of the relay API interface.

parts.name: Token and proof checks
parts.why: Verify relay tokens and DPoP proofs for the handlers (infra/relay/src/auth), guards with only replay markers of their own.

parts.name: Account deletion
parts.why: Reacts to the identity service's deletion webhook by deleting the other parts' rows (infra/relay/src/accounts/AccountDeletion.ts).

parts.name: Mobile crash telemetry
parts.why: Forwards mobile traces and logs to maintainers (infra/relay/src/mobileTelemetry), tooling.

parts.name: Persistence and wiring
parts.why: Postgres schema, queues and worker setup (infra/relay/src/persistence, db.ts, queues.ts, worker.ts).

components.name: Environment connections
components.description: Links environments to accounts, allocates their managed tunnels, and runs the flow that admits a client to a linked environment.

parts.name: Endpoint failure helpers
parts.why: Shared error mapping (infra/relay/src/environments/endpointFailure.ts).

components.name: Account links
components.description: Keeps which environment is linked to which account and with which key, refuses unsafe relinks, and runs the connect flow.

parts.name: T3 Chat plan check
parts.why: Asks T3 Chat for the plan when an account hits its default cap and stores no copy (infra/relay/src/t3chat/T3ChatAccounts.ts), an adapter.

components.name: Managed tunnels
components.description: Allocates, recovers and reclaims the public tunnels of linked environments, guarding each change with a generation.

parts.name: Reaper and upstream pause
parts.why: Clean-up of idle tunnels and back-off from the Cloudflare API (ManagedEndpointReaper.ts, CloudflareApiPause.ts).

components.name: Mobile notifications
components.description: Keeps the phones registered for alerts and Live Activities and the latest agent activity, and decides and delivers push notifications.

parts.name: Registrations
parts.why: Devices and Live Activities (agentActivity/Devices.ts, LiveActivities.ts); the core store.

parts.name: Activity and alerts
parts.why: Aggregate activity and decide alerts (agentActivity/AgentActivityPublisher.ts, agentActivityAlerts.ts).

parts.name: Deliveries
parts.why: APNs and FCM queues that also drop dead tokens from the registrations (agentActivity/Apns*.ts, Fcm*.ts), so they share the store.

components.name: Held webhooks
components.description: Gives webhook senders a stable URL, forwards their calls to the environment, and holds them in order while it is offline.

parts.name: Forwarder and inbox
parts.why: One Durable Object store per link (hooks/HookForwarder.ts, HookInboxObject.ts, HookInboxStore.ts).

outsideServices.name: Coding agents
outsideServices.description: The coding agents T3 Code runs and their vendors' services: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx and ACP Registry agents.

outsideServices.name: Model APIs
outsideServices.description: Hosted model APIs, such as OpenAI, xAI and OpenRouter, used for text generators and cloud transcription.

outsideServices.name: Usage quota sources
outsideServices.description: A CLIProxyAPI hub or the user's own HTTP quota server that reports subscription limits.

outsideServices.name: Code hosting services
outsideServices.description: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Forgejo and Gitea, GitCafe, TanStack Source and Cursor Origin.

outsideServices.name: Linear
outsideServices.description: The Linear issue tracker, connected with an API key.

outsideServices.name: 1Password
outsideServices.description: The 1Password password manager, read through its CLI, a service account or a Connect server.

outsideServices.name: Cloudflare
outsideServices.description: Cloudflare's tunnels and DNS, which carry T3 Connect traffic to machines.

outsideServices.name: Clerk
outsideServices.description: The identity service behind T3 Connect accounts.

outsideServices.name: T3 Chat
outsideServices.description: T3 Chat, whose paid plans raise an account's T3 Connect machine limit.

outsideServices.name: Push notification services
outsideServices.description: Apple Push Notification service and Firebase Cloud Messaging.

outsideServices.name: Tailscale
outsideServices.description: The Tailscale network on the machine, used for tailnet addresses and Tailscale Serve routes.

outsideServices.name: Device services
outsideServices.description: Remote device hosts reached over SSH, Simlock gateways and Expo's EAS builds.

outsideServices.name: SSH hosts
outsideServices.description: Remote Linux or Mac machines the desktop app reaches over SSH to run a T3 Code server.

resources.name: Environment
resources.description: One running T3 Code server and the machine, projects and agents it controls.

resources.name: Environment connection
resources.description: An environment an app has saved, with how it reaches it and the app's credential for it.

resources.name: Project

questions.question: Is T3 Connect its own Level 1 provider?
questions.answer: Part of T3 Code rather than its own provider; the relay has its own deployment and data, but no consumers of its own, since the developer turns it on from T3 Code's settings to reach their own machines, and the rule asks for all three.

questions.question: Are outside agents and bots on the MCP server a consumer of their own?
questions.answer: Another interface of the Developer rather than a separate consumer; the developer signs each one in and picks its level, so they act for the developer, although a hosted bot's operator also gets the access.

questions.question: Is the client app a component or only interfaces?
questions.answer: A Level 2 component rather than interfaces alone, because it keeps the saved environments and their credentials, which only it changes; inside it only that connection runtime passes the test, so it stays closed.

questions.question: One outside service per vendor, or grouped?
questions.answer: Grouped as Coding agents (with the ACP Registry), Code hosting services, Model APIs and Device services rather than one per vendor; each group sits behind one contract on T3 Code's side, and splitting would repeat identical boundaries.

questions.question: Is updating T3 Code a capability?
questions.answer: Excluded as work on the system itself rather than a developer capability, though the docs give updates prominence; installing and updating agents stays a capability because agents are what the developer uses the system with.

questions.question: Are agent drivers adapters or a component?
questions.answer: A component with variants rather than adapters to outside services; each driver keeps its instances' live sessions, processes and credentials and declares their capabilities, beyond translating a protocol.

questions.question: Where do the project services belong?
questions.answer: In Orchestration rather than Workspace, because project/ProjectService.ts and the session importer commit through Orchestration's EventSink and ProjectStore.

questions.question: Should Settings and policy open?
questions.answer: Opened into Environment settings and Policy enforcement rather than kept as one component; the policy is state T3 Code never writes and alone decides limits, while settings are written by the server.

questions.question: What does a linked environment call?
questions.answer: The other machine's Agent tools, the same component in another environment, rather than a separate outside service, since it uses the same MCP contract outside agents use.

questions.question: Do direct SQL reads of Orchestration's projections break its contract?
questions.answer: Counted as reads around the contract and listed as a cleanup candidate rather than as part of Orchestration's contract; the architecture makes projections the source of truth, but these reads skip its projection and thread services.

questions.question: Are approvals, questions and secret requests a resource?
questions.answer: One resource, Agent request, rather than parts of Thread, because people list and answer them on their own, from any device.

questions.question: Are checkpoints a resource at Level 1?
questions.answer: Folded into Thread at Level 1 (Revert to an earlier turn) rather than a resource the developer manages; they appear as a resource at Level 3, where Orchestration captures and restores them.

questions.question: Are dictation, SnapShots, prompt links and drafts capabilities?
questions.answer: Interactions of writing a message at Level 1 rather than capabilities; SnapShots and dictation appear as capabilities at Level 2, where the window asks the desktop shell and the environment for them.

questions.question: Where do documentation files go in places?
questions.answer: Placed as excluded documentation rather than tooling or a component, because they are not code; they were read as evidence.

questions.question: Is Agent installation's refresh of the registry a boundary?
questions.answer: A step of installing rather than a boundary; installation would not call the registry except to finish its own install.

cleanupCandidates.name: V1 thread import
cleanupCandidates.why: Copies and migrates the V1 database into V2 once, with its legacy tables and toast (orchestration-v2/legacy, persistence/ProviderSessionRuntime.ts); a bridge from older versions.

cleanupCandidates.name: V2 preview id reconciliation
cleanupCandidates.why: Repairs migration ids used by V2 preview builds (persistence/reconcileV2PreviewMigration.ts); transitional.

cleanupCandidates.name: Desktop legacy local storage merge
cleanupCandidates.why: Moves the old renderer storage into the new stores (apps/desktop/src/legacyLocalStorageMerge.ts and its bridge method); transitional.

cleanupCandidates.name: Legacy auth scopes
cleanupCandidates.why: Auth responses keep the old scopes field beside exact permissions for older clients and servers (docs/internals/04_environment-auth.md); a compatibility path.

cleanupCandidates.name: Older idle compaction setting
cleanupCandidates.why: compactIdleThreads is kept beside idleCompaction (docs/user/managed-policy.md); a compatibility path.

cleanupCandidates.name: Direct reads of Orchestration's projection tables
cleanupCandidates.why: Eleven files in other components read projection tables with SQL instead of Orchestration's services (for example storageCleanup.ts, usage/CodexUsageHistory.ts, workspace/KnownWorkspaces.ts, pullRequest/linkedThreads.ts); reads around the contract.

cleanupCandidates.name: Relay account deletion
cleanupCandidates.why: Deletes rows of the environment links and mobile notification tables directly (infra/relay/src/accounts/AccountDeletion.ts); a write around those components' contracts.

excluded.name: Engineering tooling
excluded.why: Build, test, lint, typecheck, release and deploy tooling, CI, evals, the shared task cache, contributor agent skills and the dev replay provider work on the system itself.

excluded.name: Installing, updating and uninstalling T3 Code
excluded.why: The installer, t3 update, the background service, the service launcher and desktop updates set up the system itself.

excluded.name: Diagnostics and observability
excluded.why: Diagnostics pages, process and trace diagnostics, OTLP export, t3 trace, t3 doctor and relay or mobile telemetry are direct reads of the system for maintainers.

excluded.name: Product analytics and agent feedback
excluded.why: Usage events sent to T3 Code's ingest and feedback reports to the T3 team report on the system itself.

excluded.name: Clean-up jobs
excluded.why: Storage and worktree cleanup, database space reclaim and idle tunnel reclamation are machinery nobody uses for a purpose of their own.

excluded.name: Health checks and readiness probes
excluded.why: Provider probes, environment and relay health checks are machinery.

excluded.name: Provider behavior
excluded.why: Auto-settling threads, idle compaction, keep-awake, restart continuation, resuming after usage limits and writing titles are things T3 Code does on its own.

excluded.name: Interactions folded into capabilities
excluded.why: Dictation, SnapShots, prompt links, the prompt stash, uploads, choosing a machine for a draft, the welcome page and opening links in T3 Code are steps of sending a message, starting a thread or using the browser.

excluded.name: Device-only preferences
excluded.why: Appearance, themes, keyboard focus and notification switches are settings of one device, not resources.

excluded.name: Informational pages
excluded.why: Open source licenses and legal pages are information, not capabilities.

excluded.name: Vendored repositories, generated code and lockfile
excluded.why: Dependencies and generated output are outside the corpus.
